name: Qing Yao
role: PhD Student in Speech & Audio Processing
bio: I'm a PhD student at Jiangsu University working on diffusion-based generative models for speech enhancement, particularly Schrödinger bridges and masked diffusion models. Speech enhancement is inherently an ill-posed inverse problem, where a degraded observation may correspond to multiple plausible clean-speech signals. My research explores generative approaches to address this ill-posedness while balancing reconstruction fidelity, perceptual naturalness, and computational efficiency.

education.description: Research in diffusion-based generative modeling and speech enhancement.

news.html: Our paper “Regularized Schrödinger Bridge via Distortion-Perception Perturbation for High-Fidelity Speech Enhancement” is accepted to IEEE/ACM TASLP.
The preprint “Regularized Schrödinger Bridge via Distortion-Perception Perturbation for High-Fidelity Speech Enhancement” was released on arXiv, with open-source code and an interactive audio demo.
Began research on Speech Enhancement: applying diffusion generative modeling to address the ill-posedness of the underlying audio inverse problem.
Began research on Dialogue-Based Relation Extraction: entity modeling and relation mining in text knowledge extraction.

projects.name: RSB
projects.description: Regularized Schrödinger Bridge (RSB) — a generative speech enhancement approach that reconciles fidelity and realism while mitigating exposure bias, via Distortion-Perception Perturbation regularized training.

projects.name: RSB Audio Demo
projects.description: Interactive listening demo: compare Measurement, Ground Truth, NCSN++M, StoRM, SB, and RSB on denoising (WSJ0+WHAM) and dereverberation (WSJ0+REVERB) samples, with waveforms.
